newsitem.title: INDIA: India contracts for 1.25 mln tonnes wheat - STC.
newsitem.headline: India contracts for 1.25 mln tonnes wheat - STC.

text.p: India's state-run State Trading Corporation (STC) said on Wednesday it has contracted to import 1.25 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (April-March), with the first shipments expected to arrive later this month.
"We have till now contracted for 1.25 million tonnes of wheat," STC director Deepak Prasad told Reuters.
"First shipments are expected to arrive later this month," Prasad said.
India last month decided to import two million tonnes of wheat in the current financial year to augment domestic supplies and check rising prices.

India last imported wheat in 1992/93, buying two million tonnes of wheat. It exported 600,000 tonnes in 1995/96 and 1.07 million tonnes between April and September of this year, when the government halted exports.
Prasad said India was focusing on Argentina, Australia and Canada as suppliers.
He declined to provide any details about the remaining 750,000 tonnes of wheat to be imported.

Prasad denied a newspaper report that STC had asked the government for an additional month's time to import the wheat. The Business Line newspaper said STC had asked to have until April 30, instead of March 31, to import the wheat.
"We have absolutely not sought extension," Prasad told Reuters.
He said STC would be able to import the two million tonnes of wheat by the end of the financial year, which concludes on March 31.
